judgments.label: false_positive
judgments.rationale: The element is the "VLibras" text link (sign-language icon is aria-hidden) in the header accessibility list next to "Alto Contraste", pointing to http://www.vlibras.gov.br/, which now redirects to the gov.br page of VLibras. VLibras is the proper name of the federal Libras translation tool, and the link leads to that tool's own site, so the link text names its destination; Understanding 2.4.4 accepts the name of the destination as link text. The claim that the text does not tell where the link goes is therefore not true of the capture, and the link meets 2.4.4. The live server HTML has the same link (the snapshot adds target="_blank", which does not touch the claim), so the capture does not differ in a way that matters. The model had the text and the href and misjudged a proper name as uninformative.

judgments.label: false_positive
judgments.rationale: The element is the h5 "JAI" section heading. Under it are three news items about the JAI (Jornada Acadêmica Integrada, UFSM's annual academic event): "Segundo dia da 41ª JAI reúne trabalhos...", "...palestra marca abertura da JAI na UFSM/FW" and an SAE item from the same event, plus a "+ JAI" link to posts tagged jai; the screenshot shows the same. The heading names the topic of all the content under it, so the claim that it says nothing about that content is false, and the heading meets 2.4.6; not expanding the acronym is a matter for 3.1.4 (AAA), not 2.4.6. The live page has the same section, so no capture difference matters. The model misread a short event name as non-descriptive.

judgments.label: false_positive
judgments.rationale: Row with no claim. The element is the link "Ministério da Mulher, da Família e dos Direitos Humanos" in the gov.br bar's "Órgãos do Governo" list, href http://www.mdh.gov.br/. The link text names the ministry whose site the address belongs to, so its purpose can be determined from the text alone; the ministry has since been renamed, which is a content-currency issue, not a 2.4.4 failure. No other link shares the name. mdh.gov.br did not answer from here (connection timed out), but the destination is not needed to see that the text states the purpose. The bar is injected by barra.js, and the live barra.js still writes the same link, so the capture does not differ. The element meets 2.4.4, so Rampa missed nothing.

judgments.label: true_positive
judgments.rationale: The element is the photo in the first "Galerias de fotos" carousel slide, alt "Descubra UFSM (Foto: Jessica Mocellin)", inside a link that opens the full-size photo, with a visible caption repeating the same words. The crop shows students around a stand with a globe and leaflets; the alt gives only the gallery series name and the photographer credit, nothing the picture shows, so the claim, read in good faith, points at the real defect: the alternative does not convey the photo's content. In a photo gallery the photos are the content, and the same title-plus-credit pattern is reused on the other slides (seven say "Foto: Mathias Ilnicki"), so a screen-reader user cannot tell the photos apart or learn what they show; the image fails 1.1.1. The live HTML has the same img and alt, so the capture does not differ in a way that matters (the screenshot shows a later carousel position).

judgments.label: true_positive
judgments.rationale: The element is the UFSM coat-of-arms image, the only content of <a title="Logotipo UFSM" href="/"> (the home page). Its alt, "Imagem do brasão composta por quatro elementos: escudo, flor de lis, archotes e lema.", describes the emblem's parts and names neither UFSM nor the home page, so replacing the image with it (G82) does not tell users where the link goes; the claim is true of the capture. By R2, neither the title "Logotipo UFSM" (a description, not the image's alternative; Chrome's tree names the link from the alt and exposes the title as description) nor the adjacent "UFSM Universidade Federal de Santa Maria" text link to the same address cures 1.1.1: H30 requires the alternative of an image that is a link's only content to describe the link's function. The live HTML has the same markup. True positive.
